baer-heitev/1:א: (א) There is no lawyer. "And thou, ," he said. It is written that Heaven’s Word is given to Heaven’s Word:
baer-heitev/1:ב: (ב) To write. Scripture verses and a letter of peace and reminding him of his debts, and likewise anything not requiring great study. Mateh Moshe, Beit Yosef, Orach Chayyim.
baer-heitev/2:_: Not a custom. And in the words of Heaven’s Word, Heaven’s Word is the same:
baer-heitev/3:_: In eulogy. A place where the custom is that on the seventh day they go to the grave to lament — it is forbidden on Purim except the mourner alone goes there with one chazan and he says hashkavah to him. Even on erev Purim it is forbidden to go there lest people think mourning ceased because of Purim. R' Shimon Halevi siman 13, Knesset HaGedolah.
baer-heitev/4:א: (א) To hear. It requires study, for Rabi did not rule in Sefer HaZekhirim that he not leave his house — if so he should have written in the language of "some say" etc. Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/4:ב: (ב) Fathers. In the Gemara and the petitioner, they testified that the custom was to mourn and that the congregation and now Grim was on the ground against the barbarians and that all kinds of joy should not be seen. M:
baer-heitev/4:ג: (ג) In private. He prays in his house and afterward goes to the synagogue to hear Megillah — Tur and so in Levush; however it implies in Tur that in the morning he goes to the synagogue for prayer — see Yoreh Deah siman 393. Magen Avraham. Taz wrote: it appears to me that since there is no mourning on Purim in public, one should not read in the synagogue on Motzei Shabbat before Barchu to walk opposite the mourner, for one should not mention the mourner's name in public; rather he goes to the synagogue without reading — end of his words.
baer-heitev/4:ד: (ד) for me. My nose is shot. M:
baer-heitev/6:_: dishes. My nose in seven of them will not send any kind of phenomens that they do to make fun of the X-Men. And he wrote that he would not send to the Babylonian Father anything that is not to be happy and that he would not be able to receive a single word from his relatives or to one of the matters, and that he would simply say that he would be reluctant to send him out of the dust of his hand. A:
baer-heitev/7:א: (א) At night. “Look at me, O Heaven, I will not eat meat and I will see it at night and so on.”
baer-heitev/7:ב: (ב) First. It is written by Dr. D. D. D. K. D. K. D. K. D. K. K. K. D. K. K.D. and is used for the departure. And from above, Heaven’s mercy will be revealed. A:
baer-heitev/8:א: (א) To marry. baer-heitev/8:ב: (ב) You won't be cheap. It is possible to welcome what is decorated with Heaven. machatzit-hashekel/1:_: (s.k. 1) In all places Orach Chayyim 568 — through a gentile it is permitted on erev Purim, all the more on Purim which is lighter. For one who does melacha on erev Purim they put him in cherem; one who does on Purim they do not put him in cherem.
machatzit-hashekel/2:א: (א) It is not the same as Heaven’s Word, nor is it possible for Heaven’s people to do it. All the wise men who do as Dr. S. K. K. K. K. K. K. K. A. A. A. A. A.A. means that he does not see and does not mention any of the custom:
machatzit-hashekel/2:ב: (ב) But in Beit Yosef it implies etc., that he wrote Rambam's proof is from the incident of Rav who saw that man sowing flax on Purim; and he erred and the flax did not sprout — behold it appears he does not see a sign of blessing. If so there is no proof except for a place that practiced prohibition, for the gemara there challenges on what it concludes there that prohibition of melacha was not accepted and it is permitted by law — if so why did Rav curse that man? And they answer: because of things permitted and others practiced prohibition on them. If so necessarily in the place where that man sowed there was a place that practiced prohibition on it, and in a place that did not practice prohibition there is no proof that he does not see a sign of blessing.
machatzit-hashekel/3:_: C. K. K. K. K. is not growing. And then he loses the seeds of the palm of the palm of the palm of the palm of the palm of the palm of the palm of the palm of the palm of the seed. He heard another version of him. Our goddess are proven to lose the seed:
machatzit-hashekel/8:_: (s.k. 8) Matters etc.; however it implies in Tur etc. that he wrote: and after he prays in the mourner's house on the night of Purim he goes to synagogue to hear — nevertheless end of his words. And from that he wrote on the night of Purim it implies specifically at night before prayer Purim had not yet begun — so too; but by day he is permitted to go to synagogue to pray.
magen-avraham/1:א: (א) In all places. Orach Chayyim 568 that through a gentile it is permitted; see siman 554 s.k. 22.
magen-avraham/1:ב: (ב) I don't see. “Look at the Rambam instead of being used to do so, and as such, it is written in its name in Smig, but in the Gemara it means not to do:
magen-avraham/1:ג: (ג) C. Blessings. Like if it worsens what is not a growth, but Heaven writes that he is not exalted, but he does not lose anything, and he says that he is not lost in Heaven
magen-avraham/1:ד: (ד) Orders of the walk. Heaven’s promise to Abraham and Heaven’s promise to Heaven’s mercy, and to all the things that I do
magen-avraham/3:_: Forbidden in eulogy. A place where the custom is that on the seventh day they go to the grave to lament — forbidden on Purim except the mourner alone goes there with one chazan and says hashkavah to him; even on erev Purim it is forbidden to go there lest people think mourning ceased because of Purim (R' Shimon Levi 13, Knesset HaGedolah).
magen-avraham/4:א: (א) Nevertheless he goes to synagogue. It requires study, for Rabi ruled in Sefer HaZekhirim that he not leave his house — if so he should have written in the language of "some say" etc.
magen-avraham/4:ב: (ב) And some say there is no mourning etc. Bach and Rashal and Perishah testified the custom is to mourn; and so Maharil; and now the world follows Rama's words; it appears to me one should be careful in all except removing shoes and sitting on the ground because of people, and all the more forbidden to see all kinds of joy.
magen-avraham/4:ג: (ג) Private matters etc. He prays in his house and afterward goes to synagogue to hear Megillah (Tur and so in Levush); however it implies in Tur that in the morning he goes to synagogue for prayer — see Yoreh Deah siman 393.
magen-avraham/4:ד: (ד) He’s given him to me. A.D. is indemnified and circumcised in the Gemara:
magen-avraham/5:_: Not out there. He said, “In the middle of the year, I will eat a third meal, but in the middle of the year, he will go to his house to eat a third meal, and he will go to the house when he is, but in the middle of the year, he will go to the house, and he will return to his house, and he will return to his father’s house
magen-avraham/6:א: (א) But he must send. It is written in the words of the Almighty that Heaven does not send to Him and that He does not send to Him, nor shall He be blessed with Him, and that He may not be blessed with Him, and that He may not be saved, and that He will not be saved, and that He will not be given to the poor
magen-avraham/6:ב: (ב) In the wake of the opinion, C.C. He said that he would not be able to pray to Heaven’s people, and that he would not be able to pray for him
magen-avraham/7:א: (א) Do a single. And he said, “I will give thanks to him.”
magen-avraham/7:ב: (ב) And all the more he is obligated. Rama's words require great study: granted in meat and wine it is permitted because of Purim joy; but Shema and prayer — the reason he is exempt is he should be free for the deceased's needs; if so what is different about Purim from weekdays? And even if one says he holds that at night he is obligated in Shema since his law is like second day of Yom Tov as written siman 688 seif 5 — nevertheless it is difficult how we learn this in what he wrote in meat and wine, what relevance does this have to that — requires study.
magen-avraham/7:ג: (ג) Specifically at night. It requires study why he should be permitted at night in meat and wine, for behold there is no obligation at all to eat at night as Rashi wrote siman 695; if so how did he write communal positive mitzvah etc.; and it is puzzling on the 14th siman 341 he ruled that even on Shabbat if he wishes not to eat meat the permission is in his hand, as Terumat HaDeshen wrote: he is not obligated to eat meat and wine etc.; what they forbade on a weekday is lest he continue after his pleasures and be nullified from burying the deceased — end of his words (and see siman 552 seif 10 that when prevented because of mourning it is forbidden); if so there is no positive mitzvah at all even by day; and it is possible to say Purim is different since it is written therein joy, and there is no joy except with meat — nevertheless it is difficult, for Yom Tov too joy is written therein and there is no obligation to eat meat except when the Temple stood — see siman 529; therefore it appears to me at night in any case he should not eat meat, for in any case there is prevention as written siman 695 seif 2 in Hagahah; and what he wrote "it appears to me specifically at night" refers to Megillah.
magen-avraham/7:ד: (ד) Buried first died. He said, “It’s hard for him to call his father’s wife, and he will not be able to do so, and he will be able to do so with him, and he will not be able to do so.” It is a sign of Heaven’s Word, and Heaven’s Word is revealed to him, and that he will be given to him, and that he will not be given to him
magen-avraham/7:ה: (ה) It is better than Shabbat. In other words, the two-year-olds were buried and in the Shabbat that you have been living in the field are exempt from all of them as “here and the congregation:
magen-avraham/8:_: Permitted to marry. On a festival it is written "and you shall rejoice in your festival" and not "with your wife," and not on Purim; and further it is one day, and because of one day a person does not delay himself, and as those who say because of cancellation of procreation (Beit Yosef in name of Rashba); superficially it implies here that granted on a festival we decree lest he delay until the festival to become intoxicated and the seven days of feasting come out on the seven days of the festival — but on Purim because of one day he will not delay — requires study, for we say in gemara it is permitted to marry on erev the festival, for because of one day a person does not delay himself (Rashi and Ran: since if he delays further he cannot do on the festival) — if so he should not set up the marriage on erev the festival, and this is not relevant regarding Purim; and it is possible Rashba's reasoning is he speaks of his own soul alone, only he seized the gemara's language; nevertheless it is difficult from where he learned this, and it is possible his proof is from that it is permitted to marry on erev Shavuot and we are not concerned he will delay the marriage until after Shavuot, for it is only one day — rather per force since it is only one day he is not concerned to delay, for in any case he must do seven days of feasting. Levush wrote per what I wrote siman 688 seif 6 one should not make the Purim feast on Shabbat — if so here too forbidden to make a wedding feast on the 14th per force; in my humble opinion it is not comparable, for there the reason is if so the Purim feast would not be recognizable; but here what matter if the wedding feast is not recognizable; see what I wrote there; but if it is difficult, this is difficult, for we hold one may not mix joy with joy as I wrote beginning siman 696 and we derive from scripture — if so how permitted to mix wedding joy with Purim joy? One could say: therefore Rashba concluded these matters are d'rabbanan and we follow leniency — meaning for those who say one may not mix, in truth it is forbidden; but since for the other view it is permitted, we follow leniency; if so per what I wrote beginning siman 696 we hold like those who say one may not mix joy with joy — here too forbidden; therefore it appears he should make the canopy on the 13th as above.
mechaber/1:main: The laws concerning bewailing, fasting and the performance of Shabbos labor on Purim, 8 Seifim : One may do work [which is forbidden on the Shabbat] on Purim, but places that have the custom not to should not, (And today, all places have the custom not to) (Kol Bo), and anyone who does [work] will never see blessing from that work, unless it is a joyful building, such as a house for a newly-married son, or an arbor for kings and officers. {Rama: And it is permitted to do work for a mitzva, such as writing Torah law decisions. And similarly it is permitted to do even work in the fullest sense for the needs of Purim (T"H Siman 112}.}
mechaber/2:main: Even in a place that has the custom [to do work], this only applies on the day of the reading of the Megillah itself. But to forbid this for that is not our custom
mechaber/3:main: The 14th and 15th are forbidden from eulogies and fasting for everyone in every place, whether for residents of a walled city who read on the 15th only or whether residents of cities who read on the 14th only. And the women, when they answer (the eulogies) all answer as one. And the kerchiefs, where they strike hand on hand. But not a professional mourner, where only one speaks and the others answer after her. They bury the dead without answering and without lamenting.
mechaber/4:main: All of the elements of mourning we observe on Chanukah and Purim: {Rama: RAMAH- never the less one goes to the synagogue to hear the megillah. If one can assemble a minyan in their home this is preferable. And there are those who say that no mourning (practices) are performed on Purim, not on the 14th or the 15th and this is the way to behave. Even the (public practices) of the first day of mourning are pushed off because of Purim but the private practices are still observed. And even though we don't (publically} observe mourning practices on Purim you can be counted for the minyan of 7 (for Torah Reading} like on Shabbat and thus ruled the Rav on his own.}
mechaber/5:main: If it is cold on Shabbat night, but sitting in the synagogue on the Shabbat, the host will not leave until he prays an Arab fall and hears a call from its time and tomorrow, the key of his home will not come out:
mechaber/6:main: One says that a mourner is still obligated in sending gifts on Purim. {Rama: One should not send gifts to a mourner during their 12 months of mourning. If one though is in a city where the only person is a mourner one is obligated to send to the mourner to fulfill the obligation of sending gifts on Purim, unless the mourner declines the gift.}
mechaber/7:main: There are those who say an onen is permitted in meat and wine, for the individual positive mitzvah of mourning does not come and override the communal d'oraisa positive mitzvah of rejoicing on Purim, which are divrei kabbalah and are like Torah law. {Rama: And all the more so he is obligated in Megillah reading and prayer and Shema; it appears to me specifically at night even though the deceased is laid before him, but by day when he wishes to bury him he buries his dead first as explained above siman 687 seif 2, and therefore reads and prays afterward, for Purim is not more important than Yom Tov and Shabbat as explained above siman 71, so it is.}
mechaber/8:main: One may marry a woman on Purim, {Rama: both on the fourteenth and on the fifteenth. All the more so, one may redeem one's firstborn (Tosfot to ch. 1 of Moed Qatan}. The custom of wearing masks on Purim, and of crossdressing, is totally permitted because of its innocent and joyful purpose, as is the wearing of shaatnez. While some would prohibit it, our practice is as I have already said. So too those who playfully rob each other do not violate "Thou shalt not steal'', and such is our custom. However, you may do only as local elders permit. (Responsum of Mahari Minz #17}.}
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (א) (a) It is permitted in the work of Heaven’s creation, and it is not possible for them to do so that they do not receive any of them to do:
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (ב) One does not do — and through a gentile it is permitted.
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (ג) (c) Everywhere you don't do, and Pramya is allowed to be happy
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (ד) (d) A sign of blessing, such as if something is not exalted, but the Gemara says that it is not exalted, but does not lose anything
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (ה) (e) or aboriginal of kings, who are not allowed to fly in his shadow:
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (ו) (b) The verses of the Gemara and the decree of peace and the mention of its obligations, and everything that I am a great reference. And it is written in the pages of the heavens to see that it should not be seen It will attract it and cancel a fruitful joy. A scroll can be written in columns:
mishnah-berurah/2:_: (c) It is not a custom – and it is necessary to be improved and it appears to be dependent on the custom of the place:
mishnah-berurah/3:א: (א) (h) In the shofar, and a place that is dying on the grave is forbidden to the grave, but the mourning alone will go there with one vision and say to him the layer and even to him In the evening of Purim, the world will not be thought that the bees have stopped in the suburbs:
mishnah-berurah/3:ב: (ט) And fasting — and regarding Torah scholar see above siman 695 seif 2 in Hagahah and in Mishna Berurah there. Law of Torah scholar before him see Yoreh Deah siman 401.
mishnah-berurah/4:א: (י) He goes to synagogue to hear etc. — and what he wrote in seif 5 at the end that the next day he does not leave his house refers when he has a minyan at home, though in general public reading is preferable.
mishnah-berurah/4:ב: (ב) (a) The Magdalene, but he will pray in his house:
mishnah-berurah/4:ג: (12) And some say there is not, etc., and so is the custom — even though Bach and other later authorities wrote that in their place the custom was to mourn; but already Sha'arei Teshuvah wrote in the name of several later authorities to be lenient and so the custom spread in these countries; and especially regarding removing shoes and sitting on the ground certainly one may be lenient b'dieved if he did not do so, as several later authorities wrote.
mishnah-berurah/4:ד: (יג) Private matters are practiced — behold Taz wrote walking from his house to prayer is forbidden also per this view, and this is not called in public for it is not recognizable he does so because of mourning; in Magen Avraham he wrote it implies in Tur that in the morning he goes to synagogue to pray; see Peri Megadim who wrote one who is lenient to behave thus did not lose; and so in Darkei Chayyim that in the morning he goes to prayer in synagogue.
mishnah-berurah/4:ה: (ה) (d) It is up to him, seven, even to death
mishnah-berurah/5:א: (טו) He does not leave from there etc. — this law Rokeach wrote, and in his place they would eat the third meal before Minchah; therefore he says when he comes to pray Minchah he does not leave from there; but for us he must go home after Minchah to eat the third meal, and at night pray Maariv and read Megillah at home if he has a minyan; and if not, he goes to synagogue while it is still day and is there for prayer and Megillah reading.
mishnah-berurah/5:ב: (טז) From his house's door — only to hear Megillah reading if he has no minyan at home, as above. Behold the Mechaber who copied Rokeach's words follows his view b'siyata dishmaya that mourning applies on Purim; but Rama already wrote above that we practice like poskim that mourning does not apply on Purim; per this, even if he has a minyan at home he goes to synagogue to hear Megillah in public [and to leave his house's door for discretionary matters — it implies from Peri Megadim one should be stringent]; all this by day, for "days of feasting and joy" is written; but at night if he has a minyan he prays and reads Megillah at home, and if not he prays at home and goes to hear Megillah in synagogue, and for reading alone he does not leave his house's door. See Darkei Chayyim that on day 15 he does not go from house to synagogue even for Shacharit prayer; nevertheless regarding removing shoes and sitting on ground it implies from poskim that even on day 15 it is not required. Levush wrote: Orach Chayyim justified the law and does not say Kaddish except before a sage in his presence after they eulogize him; and even though Orach Chayyim 395 they say Kaddish.
mishnah-berurah/6:א: (א) In the midst of Heaven’s Word, Heaven’s promise is that Heaven’s promise is to be given to Heaven
mishnah-berurah/6:ב: (ב) (b) It must be sent to dishes – indeed, all joys will not be sent and the congregation of those who die in the mornings will be sent to the next year Sending meats or meat to the poor will not only be made of joy:
mishnah-berurah/6:ג: (ג) (T) But there is no sender to Babylon – even something that is not of joy. And if the grief is poor, it is permissible to send it out of sight even in the midst of Heaven’s wrath:
mishnah-berurah/6:ד: (ד) Every month, we were to his father and his mother and his father, and the reason for peace is not to be made for a month
mishnah-berurah/6:ה: (ה) And as it is written in the Gemara, it is a sign that it is called for a parent instead of being able to make it easier to ask for them to be sent to them in a month Not in the midst of the fires, but they will not send him some kind of joy:
mishnah-berurah/6:ו: (ו) Unless the mourner forgives etc. — for one does not give a person a gift against his will.
mishnah-berurah/7:א: (א) It is called “the dead shall not be buried.”
mishnah-berurah/7:ב: (ב) It is permissible in the flesh and wine – even though the author above is used in the Purim of the Dao Sea, and as the book of taste and the Gemara has written And Ka, on the day of his joy, is filled with joy and joy, but not even at night. And then, in the second and second night, and then At night, I will not only be jealous of its time and humiliation:
mishnah-berurah/7:ג: (כה) And all the more he is obligated in Megillah etc. — meaning: just as for the mitzvah of joy of the day we defer the positive mitzvah of mourning and permitted him in meat and wine, certainly it is not fitting to exempt him at night from Megillah and other mitzvot since there is no way to bury then, similar to onen on second day of Yom Tov whom many poskim obligated in mitzvot for this reason; but one may question this: one, that on second night of Yom Tov itself there are views among poskim; another, that there at least it is Yom Tov, therefore aninut does not apply because there is no way to bury at night — unlike Purim whose main joy is by day, and at night is like other weekday nights, certainly aninut applies even if there is no way to bury then; therefore Darkei Chayyim wrote on the night of the 14th he hears Megillah reading afterward.
mishnah-berurah/7:ד: (כו) Burial of his dead first as explained etc. — meaning there it is proven not specifically a mitzvah corpse before Megillah reading — likewise any dead person who has no burying enough for his need, the one encountering him buries him first and then reads. In truth Magen Avraham already wrote many poskim dispute this and hold that for any dead person Megillah reading precedes his burial, and so they practice to bury after leaving synagogue; Magen Avraham challenged: fine for other people, but how is the onen obligated in Megillah reading — behold he is exempt from all mitzvot, and how did he fulfill through what he heard in public after he was not obligated at all? Per force Magen Avraham concludes: even though he heard the reading in public he reads it again after the dead is buried. Regarding Shema and prayer he is like other onen on weekdays: before burial he is exempt, after burial see above siman 71 in Mishna Berurah s.k. 4 there all details are explained. Regarding tefillin, view of many acharonim he does not put them on, as above siman 38 seif 5.
mishnah-berurah/7:ה: (ה) After that, R.R., but first the burial is exempt from it, and it ends with the exception of Shabbat and the High Court, and we were in the same way as they were buried and on the Shabbat when they were darkened For the burial purposes, it is then exempted from all the inventions and as such:
mishnah-berurah/8:א: (א) Permitted to marry etc. — not comparable to festival where it says "rejoice in your festival" not with your wife, unlike Purim; Magen Avraham wrote canopy on 13th and feast in evening; see Shaarei Teshuvah: in these lands custom spread for permission like Shulchan Aruch; Chemed Moshe wrote better to make canopy end of 14th and Purim feast earlier.
mishnah-berurah/8:ב: (כט) Pidyon haben — and milah, for in these there is not so much joy that one could say one may not mix joy with joy.
mishnah-berurah/8:ג: (ג) (L) The first is to see a letter written by the name of the High Court in the name of the Gemara that should be abolished in the petitions or in the joy of marriage and as such, it is written in the name of a name, and if as such, it is possible to cancel this custom, they are in the pits or in the joy of marriage and as such For man’s clothes only from a woman’s clothing and drunkenness, they can’t be protested by [Ps 119:105; 119:105;] and for the sake of the woman who dared to keep away from it:
mishnah-berurah/8:ד: (ד) It is not because of Heaven’s grace, and it is impossible to bless what is preached by Heaven’s people, and that His Spirit is exalted from dirty garments And then, he was swayed
mishnah-berurah/8:ה: (ה) We were from reading the scroll to the night of the feast that they were two nights and one day
turei-zahav/1:_: In all places not to do. It appears merchandise is permitted since it is joy for him; similar to what Beit Yosef wrote in name of Orach Chayyim that one may write a letter, ask of peace, and remind of his debts; and even though regarding Tisha B'Av merchandise is forbidden as written siman 554 — here it is different, for he may do all that is joy for him.
turei-zahav/4:_: And some say mourning does not apply etc. Superficially it implies this "some say" disputes what was written first that he goes to synagogue to hear Megillah — behold at time of prayer he should not go there — this "some say" disputes and holds he may go to synagogue even at time of prayer; and this is not so, for this "some say" is Maharam of Rothenburg whom Tur brought, and wrote there he prays at home and afterward goes to hear — nevertheless; if so this "some say" does not dispute except on what is written that mourning applies on Purim, namely doing mourning acts in public — he holds one should not do so, and going to prayer is forbidden and this is not called public for it is not recognizable he does so because of mourning. It appears to me: since there is no mourning on Purim in public, one should not read in synagogue on Motzei Shabbat before Barchu to walk opposite the mourner, for one should not mention mourner's name in public; rather he goes to synagogue without reading.
turei-zahav/6:_: And as written on the 14th. And since Rama wrote there our custom is to be lenient in asking peace, it is permitted to send him portions too; but it does not appear to rely on this unless the mourner is poor.
